evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.15: ā prīmō capite lēgis ūsque ad extrēmum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is “head”; in writings, a division of any size: a clause of a law, a section, a chapter. id quod caput est is “the main point” (Cic. Att. 1.17.4).
From Greek ἡ παράγραφος, the stroke that marked a new section; not in Lewis & Short. Traupman gives it once as feminine, once as masculine; we follow the Greek.

sources: Lewis & Short: caput
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 30, 356.
